quests.text: Speak with Mira by the doorstep.
Find Saren at the north gate. Take protection work.
Clear the fallen cart on the Alder Road.
Follow the road. Watch the alder thicket.
Break the foreman's road levy at the old kiln.
Return to Saren at the gate for your pay.
Buy honeybread from Tova for the family (8 crowns).
Bring the honeybread home. Speak with Mira.

morning: Your belt again. Hold still. You can face a knife, but not a buckle.
Bring me something from the road. Something that isn't a stone.
Saren needs a steady sword at the north gate. Come back before the soup forgets you.
contract: Two wagons turned back. A crew at the old kiln calls robbery a road levy.
Past the fallen cart, through the alders. Clear the road and their foreman. Thirty crowns, paid here. The shrine halfway is safe enough to rest.
payment: My wagons made it through. Thirty crowns, as promised.
They wore a knot of black cord. All of them.
Men find a symbol and start thinking it makes them a kingdom. Go home, Rayan. Tova still has honeybread.
bread: Eight crowns for a whole loaf. I saved the one with the crisp edge.
Mira will say it's too much.
Then tell her the baker can't count.
supper: It smells like summer! Did you find it on a tree?
A very particular tree. Tova grows it behind her oven.
Sit. Tell us the small things first.
A broken cart. A bird nesting in a helmet. A man who thought the road belonged to him.
Keep the last crust for tomorrow.
isha: Oren says the moon is a bowl. I think someone dropped it.
We should ask for a smaller one. Easier to carry.
oren: That old kiln north of the alders used to fire good clay. Shame what lives there now.
Bring me a quiet road and I'll make you a bowl that doesn't leak.
mira_repeat: The soup can wait a little. Be careful on the road.
saren_repeat: The cart, the thicket, then the kiln. Rest at the shrine if you need to.
tova_repeat: A warm loaf has better company at home than on my shelf.
shrine: You wash the dust from your hands. Health and three healing draughts restored. This is your new checkpoint.
well: A rope worn smooth by a hundred hands. Someone has left a little wooden bird on the rim.
cart: The grain sacks are cut open. A black cord has been tied around the axle, tight as a warning.
